n: In this lecture we study nitrogen-containing synthetic drugs: their toxicological significance, isolation from objects and methods of analysis. Key terms: nitrogen-containing synthetic drugs; novocaine, dicaine, lidocaine hydrochloride, dimedrol. The section on cyclodol, that is, a piperidine derivative, is given on the basis of the textbook “Analysis of Narcotic Substances”.

t: Characteristics of the group: cocaine substitutes
n: First, the characteristics of the group: cocaine substitutes. Novocaine is one of the synthetic compounds used in place of the natural alkaloid cocaine. Novocaine and dicaine were synthesised in order to avoid the poisonous and dangerous effect of cocaine on the body, that is, “cocainism”. In its action novocaine is weaker than cocaine and in medicine is regarded as a local analgesic. In the lecture, together with these substances, xicaine, dimedrol and cyclodol are also considered.

Structure and properties of novocaine. Novocaine is an ester of p-aminobenzoic acid with diethylaminoethanol. It is a white crystalline powder, freely soluble in water and ethyl alcohol, and sparingly soluble in chloroform and ether. In medicine it is used as a local analgesic. That is, novocaine is an ester formed from two components: an acid and an amino alcohol.

Novocaine poisoning and metabolism. Some people are very sensitive to novocaine: dizziness, weakness, lowered blood pressure, collapse and shock are observed. In a toxic dose, excitation of nervous activity occurs first, then paralysis of the central nervous system. In the body novocaine is broken down into p-aminobenzoic acid and diethylaminoethanol; about 2 % is excreted unchanged in the urine. It is isolated from the biological object with acidified water and acidified alcohol.

The azo dye reaction of novocaine. A solution of novocaine, under the action of solutions of sodium nitrite and naphthol, forms a red azo dye. The scheme is as follows: novocaine, through its primary amino group, reacts with nitrite, then naphthol solution is added, and a red azo dye appears. The amount of novocaine is also determined by the photoelectrocolorimetric method based on this azo dye reaction.

Novocaine: Dragendorff's reagent and TLC. Dragendorff's reagent forms characteristic rectangular red-brown crystals with novocaine. In TLC a mixture of cyclohexane, benzene and diethyl ether in the ratio 75:15:10 is used, the visualising reagent being Dragendorff's. For novocaine Rf=0.33-0.35, and for dicaine Rf=0.60-0.63. That is, in this system dicaine lies higher than novocaine.

UV spectrum of novocaine and its quantification. UV spectrum of the aqueous solution: max = 229 nm. In 2 N H2SO4 solution max = 228, 272 and 279 nm. The amount is determined by the SP method. It is also determined by the photoelectrocolorimetric method based on the azo dye reaction. In the IR spectrum, absorption bands are observed at 1690, 1274, 1605, 1174, 1116 and 772 cm⁻¹.

Let us compare novocaine and dicaine. Novocaine is the ester of p-aminobenzoic acid with diethylaminoethanol, and is weaker than cocaine. Dicaine is the ester of p-butylaminobenzoic acid with dimethylaminoethanol; it is 2 times stronger than cocaine and 10 times stronger than novocaine. Dicaine is used for anaesthesia in broncho- and oesophagoscopy and in ophthalmology. In confirmation, novocaine gives a red azo dye, while dicaine gives a red colour in the Vitali-Morin reaction. Rf values in TLC: novocaine 0.33-0.35, dicaine 0.60-0.63.

t: The essence of the photoelectrocolorimetric method
n: The essence of the photoelectrocolorimetric method. Photocolorimetry is based on the analysis of a substance by measuring in the visible part of the spectrum under polychromatic radiation. The spectrum of maximum light absorption of the coloured solution should correspond to the minimum light absorption of the light filter. For novocaine the photoelectrocolorimetry is carried out as follows: the azo dye reaction is performed, the light absorption of the solution is measured with different light filters, and the results are recorded in the lab notebook.

Structure and potency of dicaine. Dicaine is the ester of p-butylaminobenzoic acid with dimethylaminoethanol; a white or yellow crystalline substance. It is freely soluble in water, chloroform and ethyl alcohol, and poorly soluble in ethyl ether. Dicaine is highly poisonous: it acts 2 times more strongly than cocaine and ten times more strongly than novocaine. In poisoning, the signs seen in cocaine poisoning appear.

Use and isolation of dicaine. Dicaine is used for anaesthesia in broncho- and oesophagoscopy and in ophthalmology. To isolate it, extraction with organic solvents is carried out in an alkaline medium. In the body dicaine undergoes metabolism and is excreted in the urine.

Identifying dicaine. Dicaine gives the Vitali-Morin reaction, forming a blood-red colour. With 30 % NaNO2 solution it forms characteristic prismatic crystals. In the UV spectrum a solution in 0.1 N H2SO4 has max = 229, 281 and 312 nm; TLC as for novocaine. The amount of dicaine is determined by the SP and photoelectrocolorimetric methods.

Now the properties of xicaine, that is, lidocaine hydrochloride. This is a bitter-tasting white or slightly yellowish crystalline powder: readily soluble in water, 95 % alcohol and acetone, insoluble in ether. It melts at 128-129 °C. The preparation is unstable to light: on prolonged exposure it oxidises and turns yellow.

Toxicological significance of lidocaine. The excitability of the central nervous system increases: severe headache, euphoria, drowsiness and photophobia are observed. Hearing deteriorates, and paralysis of the lips and tongue and of the respiratory muscles occurs. Body temperature falls, a feeling of fever and shivering appear; severe cardiac insufficiency, that is, collapse, develops. Allergic reactions are also possible: itching, swelling, erythema.

Identifying lidocaine. The identity test is based on the azo dye formation reaction. Xicaine, under the action of cobalt nitrate solution, on standing a little forms a crystalline precipitate of blue-green colour. By UV spectrophotometry the maximum absorption falls at wavelengths of 235-269 nm.

Structure and properties of dimedrol. Dimedrol is a compound of the β-dimethylaminoethyl benzhydrol ether type; a fine white crystalline powder of bitter taste that numbs the tongue. It is freely soluble in water, 95 % ethyl alcohol and chloroform, sparingly soluble in acetone, and insoluble in diethyl ether. In medicine it is used as an antihistamine drug in the form of an injectable solution and tablets.

Action of dimedrol and toxicomania. Besides its antihistamine action, dimedrol has local anaesthetic, muscle-relaxant, antispasmodic, neuroleptic, hypnotic and antiemetic effects. It is also used in asthma together with ephedrine and euphyllin. Because it potentiates the effect of barbiturates, narcotic and psychotropic substances, drug addicts and toxicomaniacs consume it in large amounts.

Dimedrol poisoning and metabolism. In poisoning, dry mouth, difficulty in breathing, loss of consciousness and taste sensation, dizziness and headache, and thirst are observed; a tendency to it develops quickly. The pathomorphological data are unclear. Dimedrol is rapidly absorbed in the body and binds to blood plasma proteins; the mean elimination period is 3-10 hours. About 2-4 % is excreted unchanged in the urine. 72-98 % binds to plasma proteins.

t: Isolating dimedrol from blood and urine
n: Isolating dimedrol from blood and urine. Blood or urine is brought to pH=10 with ammonia and extracted twice with chloroform. The layers are combined and passed through a filter of anhydrous Na2SO4; the chloroform is evaporated until 0.5 ml remains. From the biological object, the alkaline isolate obtained by the acidified water and alcohol method is examined for dimedrol.

Dimedrol: colour reactions with acids. With concentrated H2SO4 a yellow colour forms, which after a while turns brick-red; if water is added, the complex breaks down and the colour disappears. With a mixture of concentrated H2SO4 and HNO3 a red colour forms; if water is added it becomes brown, yellow, orange, while the chloroform layer becomes violet. After the chloroform isolate is evaporated, the reagents are applied dropwise to the residue.

Dimedrol: Marquis, Liebermann and Mandelin reagents. With Marquis reagent, in the residue in a porcelain dish, a lemon-yellow colour forms. Under the action of Liebermann's reagent an orange colour appears. Under the action of Mandelin's reagent it gives a yellow colour.

Dimedrol: TLC, UV and IR. In TLC a mixture of chloroform, acetone and 25 % ammonia in the ratio 12:24:1 is used, then concentrated H2SO4 is sprayed: dimedrol gives a yellow spot, Rf=0.58-0.60. Its metabolite benzhydrol forms a spot with Rf=0.76-0.80. In the UV spectrum a solution in 0.1 N H2SO4 has max = 252 and 257 nm. In the IR spectrum 713, 754, 991, 1103, 1017, 1180 cm⁻¹.

Quantitative analysis of dimedrol. A photoelectrocolorimetric, extraction-photometric method is used in the presence of the indicator eriochrome black. By the spectrophotometric method it is determined in the region of maximum light absorption using a solution in 0.1 N sulphuric acid. Extraction photocolorimetry is based on the formation of an associate with bromothymol blue; this is given for cyclodol, 297 nm, layer thickness 20 mm.

Now the description of cyclodol. Cyclodol is a drug belonging to the piperidine derivatives: a white crystalline powder, poorly soluble in water and sparingly soluble in alcohol. It has an anticholinergic action; in medicine it is used in the treatment of Parkinson's disease. In the treatment of chronic alcoholism it is also used together with etaperazine. Cyclodol undergoes metabolic changes; mainly its metabolites are excreted in the urine, and partly the unchanged substance.

Cyclodol as a toxicomanic agent. In recent years cyclodol has begun to be used as a toxicomanic agent owing to its intoxicating, stupefying and hallucinogenic properties. Acute poisoning proceeds in four stages: euphoria, loss of consciousness, hallucinations and recovery from them. Drug addicts use it mainly to bring about the first, euphoria, and the third, hallucination, phases. Most often they begin to take it after becoming acquainted with other substances, that is, hashish, barbiturates and alcohol.

Habituation to cyclodol and withdrawal. The first phase usually develops when the therapeutic dose is exceeded 2-3 times, that is, when 4-8 tablets are taken. Habituation to cyclodol develops over 1-1.5 months; drug addicts may take up to 30-40 tablets a day. The syndrome of psychic dependence forms quickly; without treatment painful withdrawal lasts up to 7-12 days. With increasing doses, psychoses may occur.

t: Isolating cyclodol from blood and urine
n: Isolating cyclodol from blood and urine. Blood, 10 ml, is acidified with 0.02 N H2SO4 to pH=2, stirred for 2 hours and centrifuged. Then a 50 ml portion is treated with chloroform at pH=7.5 with NaOH. By this method 41-43 % of the cyclodol is isolated from the blood. Urine, 50 ml, is acidified with 20 % H2SO4 to pH=2 and treated in the same way, then extracted with chloroform.

Chemical identification of cyclodol. Cyclodol forms precipitates of various colours and physical states with general precipitating reagents. With p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde it gives a red-pink colour; with Marquis reagent, a light brown-violet colour. With Mandelin's reagent a light brown-green colour forms.

Cyclodol: isolation and analytical indicators. Blood, 10 ml, is acidified with 0.02 N and 20 % H2SO4 to pH=2 and stirred for 2 hours. Urine, 50 ml, is acidified with 20 % H2SO4 to pH=2 and treated in the same way. From biological objects, the alkaline isolate obtained by the acidified water and alcohol methods is analysed.

Cyclodol: TLC and spectra. In TLC, Sorbfil and Silufol plates are used; the system is diethylamine and dioxane, 1:490. Dragendorff's reagent modified according to Munier gives a red-brown spot, Rf=0.50-0.52. In the UV spectrum a solution in 0.1 M HCl has absorption maxima at 252, 258 and 264 nm. IR spectrum in KBr: 702, 756, 973, 1206, 1196, 935 cm⁻¹; mass spectrum: 98, 105, 55, 41, 99, 77, 218, 84 m/z.

Quantitative analysis of cyclodol. The amount is determined by UV spectrophotometry. In GLC or HPLC methods the sorbent Chromaton N - Super, 3 % methylsilicone oil SP-2100 or 5 % polymethylphenylsiloxane OV-17 is used; the detection limit is 2 µg. It is also determined by the extraction-photocolorimetric method based on the associate with bromothymol blue.

Now let us compare the TLC indicators. Novocaine Rf=0.33-0.35 and dicaine Rf=0.60-0.63; system cyclohexane, benzene and diethyl ether, 75:15:10. Dimedrol Rf=0.58-0.60, metabolite benzhydrol Rf=0.76-0.80; system chloroform, acetone and ammonia, 12:24:1. Cyclodol Rf=0.50-0.52; system diethylamine and dioxane, 1:490.

Now let us compare the UV spectrum indicators. Novocaine: 229 nm in water; 228, 272, 279 nm in 2 N H2SO4. Dicaine: 229, 281, 312 nm in 0.1 N H2SO4. Dimedrol, 0.1 N H2SO4: 252, 257 nm. Lidocaine: maximum in the range 235-269 nm. Cyclodol, 0.1 M hydrochloric acid: 252, 258, 264 nm.

The general scheme of analysis. First, extraction from blood and urine is carried out; from the biological object an alkaline isolate is obtained by the acidified water or alcohol method. For confirmation, colour and precipitation reactions, crystal reactions, TLC, and UV and IR spectra are used. The amount is determined by SP, photoelectrocolorimetry, extraction photometry, GLC and HPLC.

Let us compare the isolation of dimedrol and cyclodol. Dimedrol: blood or urine is brought to pH=10 with ammonia and extracted twice with chloroform. Cyclodol: blood is acidified to pH=2, then extracted with chloroform at pH=7.5. For both substances, the alkaline isolate obtained by the acidified water and alcohol method is examined.

Let us review the identity reactions. Novocaine with sodium nitrite and naphthol forms a red azo dye. Dicaine gives a blood-red colour in the Vitali-Morin reaction. Lidocaine gives a blue-green precipitate with cobalt nitrate. Dimedrol gives a yellow, then brick-red colour in concentrated H2SO4. Cyclodol gives a red-pink colour with p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde.

t: Continuation of the lecture outline: other drug groups
n: Continuation of the lecture outline. The outline: nitrogen-containing synthetic drugs, their toxicological significance, methods of isolation and analysis. Other items of the outline: antidepressants, diuretics and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Key words and terms: novocaine, dicaine, xicaine, furosemide, ethacrynic acid, indomethacin, ibuprofen, ketotifen.

Conclusion. Novocaine and dicaine are synthetic local anaesthetics, cocaine substitutes: novocaine gives a red azo dye, dicaine the Vitali-Morin reaction. Lidocaine, that is, xicaine, gives a blue-green precipitate with cobalt nitrate; dimedrol gives a yellow, then brick-red colour in concentrated H2SO4. Cyclodol is used as a toxicomanic agent; Rf=0.50-0.52 and UV 252, 258, 264 nm.
